Use mathematical induction to prove that
$\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}^{n} = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 - 2^{n} \\ 0 & 2^{n}\end{bmatrix}$
for all $n ∈ N$.

We proceed using induction on $n$.

**Base Case**: We first prove that our statement is true for the base case $n =$ {{field-1}}.

For the left-hand side, we have
$\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}^{1}$ {{field-2}} {{field-3}}

and for the right-hand side, we have

$\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}^{1}$ {{field-4}} {{field-5}}

Thus, our statement is {{field-6}} for $n = 1$.
